items.detail: Logged per the 'Critical severity, always' classification so it stays visible at batch end. items.issue: Requirements ambiguity: PRD Success Metric 2 says 'a request without the local token ... is rejected before any filesystem access', but the Feature Behavior text scopes the token to '/api/* mutating routes'. The design doc self-flagged this as an open Question and never resolved it, leaving GET /api/zettels/{path}, GET /api/queries*, POST /api/queries/{name}/exec and GET /api/events unauthenticated.

Whether GET reads should also require the token is a PRD-level call recorded here for batch end.

items.issue: release_claim(sha) in the new finally is not ownership-scoped: a worker whose ingest outran claim_max_age_minutes and had its claim legitimately reclaimed by a second worker still deletes the row on exit, wiping the new owner-s live claim and letting a third run start concurrently on the same document. No claim token or owner id exists to make the release conditional.
items.reason: Fix needs a lease token/generation column on claims plus compare-and-delete release - a schema change and a new ownership concept, against a PRD that says no schema change. Raised as design-review non-blocker 1 and deliberately not applied. Needs concurrency AND a job outrunning the 60-minute TTL. Follow-up PRD.

items.issue: The PRD requires the max age to exceed a slow OCR/LLM ingest ceiling; no such ceiling exists. ocr.py shells out via subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, check=False) with no timeout=, so an ingest is unbounded. A hung or slow ocrmypdf past the 60-minute default gets its live claim stolen and the document processed twice.
items.reason: Correct reading of the PRD wording. Fix is to bound the ocrmypdf subprocess, changing OCR failure semantics in a module this PRD does not touch, with no acceptance criterion here. Design doc chose 60 minutes as a ceiling above the observed worst case, not a tight SLA. Follow-up PRD owning OCR timeouts.

items.issue: RESIDUAL of the cycle-1 Critical: no command exists to clear a processed row, so a triage proposal the human rejects or deletes leaves that raw source sha permanently un-ingestable. The PRD nice-to-have names bim doc claims --clear, which targets the claims table, but the blocking row lives in processed - the named mitigation would not fix it.
items.reason: PARTIALLY FIXED in cycle-1 rework task D1: the dangerous half (user told the document was already filed when nothing was filed) is closed by the design-specified _triage/{basename} (pending review) canonical_filename plus a pending-specific duplicate sidecar. Residual is the missing escape hatch, which is the PRD-s own explicit Nice to have and the design doc-s explicitly accepted out-of-scope risk. items.issue: Crash windows between os.replace and record_processed on both the _file_document and _triage paths. Now that the claim releases on any exit, a crash in that window leaves either a filed PDF with no dedup row (same source re-files a second archive copy) or a _triage PDF with no proposal and no staging file (unfileable). A retry also dies in sha256_file on the moved staging path.
items.reason: Real consequence of task 2, but the PRD explicitly chose release-on-any-exit. Closing the window properly needs the file move and the dedup row to commit together, a filesystem+SQLite two-phase problem. Narrowing park-forever to a narrow double-file window is a strict improvement on pre-PRD behaviour. The _triage ordering predates this PRD. Follow-up PRD.

items.issue: Two promote-path findings from Bob: (a) promote trusts the editable proposal source.sha256 and record_processed uses INSERT OR REPLACE, so an altered sha can overwrite another document-s processed identity; (b) the filed-sha and raw-source-sha rows are separate autocommit writes after files have moved, so a failure on the second leaves split metadata and an unretryable proposal.
items.reason: (a) The .proposed.yml is deliberately human-editable and promote already trusts every other field in it (issuer slug, doc type, dates all flow into the filed artifact); singling out sha256 without a wider proposal-integrity story is inconsistent. (b) Matches the codebase-s single-statement autocommit style throughout StateDB - only _migrate wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT; atomicity needs a transaction helper on StateDB. Both to a follow-up PRD.

items.issue: Oversized functions this diff edited, confirmed against the computed mechanical-facts block: Pipeline._triage 111 lines, Pipeline.run 58, CommandPromote._finalize 88 - all over the repo-s 50-line limit. Bob additionally flagged newly added tests at 62/61/73/63/109 lines.

items.issue: Two deliberate-semantics objections to the claim predicate: the stale check fails open on an unparsable claimed_at (a corrupt row lets a live claim be stolen), and is_claim_stale reports True for an already-processed sha that claim() then refuses to reclaim, so predicate and reclaimability disagree.
items.reason: Both are the chosen semantics, not drift. Fail-open is documented at the call site: a stamp no parser accepts cannot vouch for a live worker, so reading it as abandoned avoids reinstating the park-forever failure the PRD opened with, and the narrow exception contract is scoped to ValueError so a database fault still propagates. The predicate/claim disagreement is pinned by test_stale_claim_on_processed_sha_is_not_reclaimed: the predicate answers the age question the PRD asks it to export, while claim() adds a separate and correct processed-sha guard.

items.issue: shlex.quote is defeated at runtime: ShellAdapter.exe runs os.path.expandvars over the whole command AFTER the caller quoted it (shell.py:53-54, 125-134), and expandvars is quote-unaware. A filename containing $VAR injects (proven live by the blind lens), and dot rm '$HOME' acts on the wrong file. This defeats quoting at every shlex.quote-guarded call site in dot, not just rm.py.
items.reason: Orchestrator-verified by direct read of shell.py:53-54 and 125-134. Deferred as HIGH rather than treated as this PRD's CRITICAL because it is PRE-EXISTING and mitigated, not introduced: before this PRD rm.py had no quoting at all, so every metacharacter injected; after it, only $VAR-bearing names do. The fix must narrow expansion to the alias body inside ShellAdapter, which changes behaviour for all 11 cfg-alias callers plus every other ShellAdapter consumer and breaks test_shell_adapter.py:250, which pins the vulnerable behaviour - well outside this PRD's declared 'single file plus its test' scope. Durable home created: dev/local/prds/backlog/00078-dot-quoting-holds-end-to-end-v1.md. The half that IS in scope - the CHANGELOG claiming the injection hole is closed - is corrected in this cycle's rework.

items.issue: dot delete still interpolates the filename unquoted into two shell=True commands (cfg rm {path}, cfg secret remove -c {path}) - the identical injection hole this PRD fixed in rm.py, attached to the command that destroys files.
items.reason: Real and pre-existing. Explicitly out of scope: the PRD scopes to rm.py plus its test and the design doc's Risks section already names delete.py as a known follow-up. Folded into the same durable home, dev/local/prds/backlog/00078-dot-quoting-holds-end-to-end-v1.md.

items.issue: Two quoting-adjacent gaps settled at the design gate: no -- end-of-options separator (a file named -c re-enables the destructive ciphertext-deleting mode this PRD removed), and git pathspec glob magic (a filename containing * is expanded by git after the shell hands it over).
items.reason: Both were raised and settled in the design doc's Risks section: shlex.quote guards shell metacharacters, not git flag or pathspec semantics, and this is pre-existing behaviour at every quoted call site in the repo (unstage.py, commit.py, git_ops.py) - not introduced or worsened by this diff. Both folded into PRD 00078, which adds the -- separator across rm and delete.

items.issue: The PRD's own example (dot rm ~/.ssh/config) never reaches the encrypted path: _is_encrypted compares the argument to cfg secret list output by exact string match, while the shell expands ~ to an absolute path and git-secret prints repo-relative paths.
items.reason: Correct, but about _is_encrypted, which this diff does not touch and which behaved identically before the PRD. Path normalisation across every dot command is the shared git-ops seam PRD 00053 already owns. Out of scope for a change whose declared surface is _remove_normal/_remove_encrypted.

items.issue: dot rm on a hidden (not revealed) secret always fails: git-secret's remove aborts with 'file not found' when the plaintext is absent, so nothing is untracked and the user sees a raw git-secret message.
items.reason: Verified against the installed git-secret 0.5.0 (bin/git-secret:1612-1615). Pre-existing behaviour of the underlying tool, unchanged by this diff, and already surfaced as a CommandResult error rather than a crash. No PRD requirement touches it.

items.issue: The new `cfg rm --cached <file>.secret` hard-fails whenever the ciphertext is not in the index: `git rm --cached` exits 128 with `fatal: pathspec did not match any files`. Reachable through dot's own TUI, where `register_secret` (tui/commands/secrets.py:59) runs `cfg secret add` only and never hides/stages, so no `.secret` is ever indexed. `dot rm` rewrites the git-secret mapping, returns failure, and tells the user to restore the mapping and retry - the retry fails identically, an unbreakable loop. Before this cycle's rework the command succeeded. Fix: `cfg rm --cached --ignore-unmatch {shlex.quote(...)}`; `_is_encrypted` already proved the file is a registered secret, so 'not in the index' is the desired end state.
items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. CONFIRMED by the orchestrator independently of the reviewers: in a throwaway repo `git rm --cached notindex.secret` exits 128, and the same command with `--ignore-unmatch` exits 0. Deferred only because the cap was reached, NOT because it was judged acceptable - it is a real regression introduced by this PRD's own cycle-1 rework and the fix is one flag wide. Raise this first at batch-end review.

items.issue: Failure to stage `.gitsecret/` still returns a successful CommandResult (only a warning is appended), so automation can commit the already-staged ciphertext removal without the mapping change that belongs with it, leaving the committed mapping stale relative to the index.
items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. Confirmed by reading rm.py:64-72 - the staging error path appends to self.warnings and falls through to success=True. Mitigating context the deferral rests on: the working-tree mapping is already correct, the failure is surfaced as a warning rather than silently swallowed, and any later `dot add .gitsecret/` repairs it. Bob rated it high; the orchestrator would rate it medium on that basis, but did not downgrade a reviewer's severity unilaterally.

items.issue: `cfg add .gitsecret/` stages the whole directory, sweeping in any unrelated pending changes there (for example keyring edits from `git secret tell`); only the mapping file that `git secret remove` touched needs staging.
items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. Real and in-scope (the staging call is new in this cycle's rework). Narrowing it to `.gitsecret/paths/mapping.cfg` is the obvious fix, but `dot encrypt` already stages `.gitsecret/` wholesale, so the broad form matches existing repo precedent and changing it is a behaviour decision rather than a defect fix.

items.issue: Untracking the ciphertext leaves `<file>.secret` on disk unignored - git-secret's `init` writes `!*.secret` into `.gitignore` - so after a successful `dot rm` the same path shows in `dot status` twice ('staged: deleted' plus 'unstaged: untracked'), and the next interactive `dot add` will offer to re-stage the blob, silently undoing the untracking. Neither dot.rst nor the CHANGELOG ('the file really does leave the repo') mentions the leftover.
items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. Both halves reproduced by Alice in a scratch repo, and the `!*.secret` negation confirmed at git-secret 0.5.0:1541-1542. Deleting the leftover is out of scope by the PRD's own success criterion (`dot rm` never deletes from disk), so the remedy is a documentation line, not a code change.

items.issue: The new recovery message tells the user to run `cfg checkout -- .gitsecret/`, but `cfg` is not a command the user has: it is an alias `ShellAdapter.alias` registers for its own subprocess call (shell.py:26-33, rm.py:24-27), documented at dot.rst:97-98 as the tool's internal alias. The runnable equivalent is `dot run checkout -- .gitsecret/`. The test at test_rm.py:223 pins the unrunnable string.
items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. In-scope and cheap - the message and its test both landed in this cycle's rework. It hands an operator a recovery command that does not exist in their shell, which is worse than no command; it should ride along with the F1 fix.

items.issue: The `.secret` suffix is hardcoded, but git-secret honours SECRETS_EXTENSION (git-secret:195); with a non-default extension the ciphertext untrack always targets a nonexistent path, so the command always fails mid-way.
items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. items.reason: Cycle 2 hit rework_cap 2 with this unresolved. items.issue: `status()` is now a mutating read path: every refresh shells out to gpg via `secret hide -m`, and `commit()` hides a second time immediately after the refresh that just hid — no dedup or throttle
items.detail: Accepted. `git secret hide -m` only re-encrypts files whose plaintext changed, so the repeat is a no-op walk in the common case. Deduplicating would need session state tracking the last hide, which costs more complexity than the saved work.

items.issue: Raw git-secret/gpg stderr is interpolated verbatim into the on-screen message, so gpg key ids and absolute paths reach the UI unfiltered and untruncated

items.issue: FileEntry.is_secret is dead in production: GitOps.status() marks it with `filepath in secrets`, but `cfg secret list` emits PLAINTEXT paths (`.ssh/config`) while `git status --porcelain` emits the tracked CIPHERTEXT path (`.ssh/config.secret`), because git-secret gitignores the plaintext. The two never match, so the TUI's file list never renders its secret marker (src/tools/dot/tui/widgets/file_list.py:92).
items.detail: Discovered during PRD 00046 cycle-1 rework, not raised by any reviewer. PRE-EXISTING: the marking logic predates this PRD; 00046 only added the hide step. Deferred as out of scope — fixing it means deciding what the TUI should show for a hidden secret (the ciphertext row, the plaintext name, or both), which is a UX decision, not a bug fix. Surfaced now because cycle 1's test-realism finding forced the old `is_secret is True` assertion to be dropped: it was passing only against a porcelain fixture production cannot produce, so positive is_secret coverage is now genuinely absent rather than fake. Candidate for PRD 00053 (dot git-ops unification) or its own PRD.

items.consensus: 2/4 (Blake correctly, Carl on a misquoted requirement)
items.issue: The automatic update path (`run_update`) still carries the 120s `_UPGRADE_TIMEOUT`; only the interactive path was raised to 1800s. A slow `uv tool upgrade` triggered by the pre-command auto-update check is still SIGKILLed at 120s, which is the half-mutated-venv hazard the PRD's own Problem section describes.
items.detail: REQUIREMENTS AMBIGUITY - needs a human call, which is why it is deferred rather than fixed. Orchestrator-verified against the pre-change file (git show b66e9c9:.../executor.py): the PRD Problem section's citation `executor.py:55-62` lands on `run_update`'s `subprocess.run(..., timeout=_UPGRADE_TIMEOUT)` and its except block - the AUTOMATIC path. The PRD's Implementation/Exports line also names `run_update()` with 'no 120s kill'. But Solution, Must-have and the Phase 0 task all say 'the interactive path', and Success Criterion 2 ('A slow upgrade is not truncated') is unqualified. The design gate read it narrowly with a documented rationale: the pre-command check must stay bounded so a scripted command is not blocked by a background upgrade. That rationale is sound; the scope question is not settled by the PRD text. Carl raised this as CRITICAL citing a requirement string ('both interactive and automatic') that does not appear anywhere in the PRD - that CRITICAL is discarded in the ledger; Blake's HIGH on a correct reading is what stands. Decide at batch end: raise the auto path to a bounded-but-generous value too, or amend the PRD to state the narrow scope explicitly. Two dependents ride with it: the test pinning `timeout: 120` on the auto path, and the auto path's fully silent TimeoutExpired branch.

items.issue: Unbounded re-exec loop: if the upgrade command exits 0 without changing the installed version (uv/pipx 'nothing to upgrade', requires-python mismatch), the re-exec'd process re-runs `check_and_update`, still reads the old `pkg_version`, upgrades and execvp's again - with no generation marker surviving the process replacement to break the cycle.
items.detail: Raised by the blind lens from code reading, not reproduced live. Structurally plausible on reading `check_and_update` (nothing re-reads the installed version after execvp, and the per-process guard cannot survive process replacement). PRE-EXISTING and out of scope: this diff touches only `_reexec_or_exit`'s OSError branch and the interactive timeout constant, neither of which sits on the success/re-exec path the loop runs through, and `updater/__init__.py` is outside the PRD's declared surface (`executor.py` only). Real and unowned - candidate for its own PRD (an env-var generation marker across execvp, or re-reading the installed version before deciding to upgrade).

items.issue: The re-exec failure message lands on stdout, not stderr as the PRD's Solution prose requires - `ConsoleAdapter` builds a Rich `Console(log_path=False)` whose default file is sys.stdout. In the PRD's own cron/pipe scenario the error contaminates the data stream. Verified end to end by the blind lens.
items.detail: Two repo requirements collide. The PRD Solution says 'print to stderr via the console adapter'; AGENTS.md mandates that ALL user-facing output route through the console adapter, and that adapter has no stderr channel. Giving it one changes output routing for every tool in the monorepo, far outside a two-task PRD scoped to executor.py. The Must-have's actual testable clause ('non-zero exit AND a user-visible message via the console adapter') is met. Batch-end decision: does the console adapter grow a stderr channel (and if so, which severities route there)?

items.issue: console.panic is annotated `-> None`, not `NoReturn`, so nothing enforces _reexec_or_exit's documented "Never returns" contract; if panic ever stops exiting, run_update returns and the command runs against a replaced venv with exit 0
items.detail: Raised by Blake. A genuine hardening, but it lives in the shared console adapter, outside this PRD's declared surface (executor.py only), and it is not neutral for the type checker: annotating panic as NoReturn makes mypy treat every statement after a console.panic(...) call as unreachable across all ~14 call sites in the monorepo, which can surface a fresh batch of errors well outside this PRD. Same class as the stdout-vs-stderr deferral - an adapter-wide change that needs its own PRD.

Pre-existing, not a regression from this PRD, and rated high rather than critical on the same calibration the gate applied to the cycle-1 instance. Deferred at rework_cap 2.
